chunks: (Abu Baseer) heard Abu Ja'far and Abu Abdillah (peace be upon them both) mentioning: When it was the Day of al-Tarwiya, Jibrail said to Ibrahim (peace be upon him):

'Quench yourself with water' — so it was named al-Tarwiya. Then he went to Mina and lodged overnight there. Then in the morning he took him to Arafat and pitched his tent at Namira, before Arafat. He built a mosque with white stones, and the traces of Ibrahim's mosque were recognizable until it was incorporated into this mosque at Namira where the Imam prays on the Day of Arafat. He prayed Zuhr and Asr there. Then he proceeded to Arafat and said: 'This is Arafat — acknowledge your rites here and confess your sins' — so it was named Arafat.

Then he departed to al-Muzdalifa — so it was named al-Muzdalifa because he approached (izdalaf) it. Then he stood at al-Mash'ar al-Haram; God commanded him to slaughter his son, while he had seen in him his noble traits and character and had grown fond of him. When morning came, he departed from al-Mash'ar to Mina and said to his mother: 'Visit the House (Kaaba) — you go — and keep the boy here.' Then he said: 'O my son! Bring the donkey and the knife so I may offer the sacrifice.' Aban said: So I asked Abu Baseer: 'What did he mean by the donkey and the knife?' He said: 'He intended to slaughter him, then carry him on it, prepare him, and bury him.'

Ismail replied: 'You will find me, if God wills, among the patient ones.' He said: When Ibrahim resolved to carry out the slaughter, [Ismail] said: 'O my father, cover my face and bind my restraints.' [Ibrahim] said: 'O my dear son, binding and slaughter together — by God, I will not combine them both upon you today!' Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: He spread the donkey's saddle-pad for him, laid him upon it, took the knife, and placed it against his throat. Then an old man came forward and said: 'What do you intend with this young man?' [Ibrahim] said: 'I intend to slaughter him.' The man said: 'Glory be to God! A youth who has not disobeyed God in the twinkling of an eye — and you would slaughter him?' [Ibrahim] said: 'Yes, God has commanded me to slaughter him.' The man said: 'Rather, your Lord has forbidden you from slaughtering him. It is only Satan who commanded you this in your dream.' [Ibrahim] said: 'Woe to you! The words I heard are what brought me to the state you see. No, by God, I will not speak to you.'

Then Ibrahim resolved again to carry out the slaughter. The old man said: 'O Ibrahim, you are indeed a leader who is emulated. If you slaughter your son, people will slaughter their children — so hold on!' But [Ibrahim] refused to speak to him. Abu Baseer said: I heard Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) saying: He laid him down at the middle Jamra, then took the knife, placed it against his throat, raised his head toward the sky, then leaned over him and pressed — but Jibrail (peace be upon him) flipped it away from his throat. Ibrahim looked and found it flipped; so Ibrahim turned it blade-side down, but Jibrail turned it spine-side up. He did this repeatedly. Then a call came from the left side of Masjid al-Khaif: 'O Ibrahim, you have indeed fulfilled the vision!' — and he pulled the young man out from beneath [the knife]. Jibrail took the ram from the summit of Thabir and placed it beneath him. The wicked old man [Satan] departed until he caught up with the old woman [Hajar] just as she was gazing at the House — the House being in the middle of the valley — and he said: 'What of an old man I saw in Mina?'

[The wicked old man Satan followed the old woman Hajar] as she was looking toward the House, the House being in the middle of the valley. He said: 'What of an old man I saw in Mina?' — and described the features of Ibrahim. She said: 'That is my husband.' He said: 'And what of a young lad I saw with him?' — and described his features. She said: 'That is my son.' He said: 'I saw him lay him down and take the knife to slaughter him.' She said: 'Never! I have never seen Ibrahim except as the most compassionate of people. How did you see him slaughtering his son?' He said: 'By the Lord of heaven and earth, and by the Lord of this sacred edifice, I truly saw him lay him down and take the knife to slaughter him.' She said: 'Why?' He said: 'He claimed that his Lord commanded him to slaughter him.' She said: 'Then it is right that he should obey his Lord.' He said: When she had completed her rites [of Hajj], she became fearful that something had befallen her son. It is as if I see her hurrying through the valley, placing her hand on her head.

When Sarah came and was informed of the news, she rushed to her son to look — and behold, there were knife-scratches on his throat! She was startled and fell ill. That was the beginning of the illness from which she died. Aban related from Abu Baseer, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), who said: He [Ibrahim] intended to slaughter him at the place where the mother of the Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) pitched her tent, near the middle Jamra. That camping ground was continually inherited from one generation to the next — great elder from great elder — until the last one who departed from it was Ali ibn al-Husayn (peace be upon him), due to a matter that arose between Bani Hashim and Bani Umayya. So he departed and pitched camp at al-Arin.

key_terms.التروية: Day of Tarwiya — the 8th of Dhul-Hijja, when pilgrims travel to Mina; named because Jibrail told Ibrahim to 'quench' (tarwiya) himself with water
key_terms.الجمرة الوسطى: The middle jamra — one of the three stone pillars at Mina, associated with the stoning of Satan during Hajj
key_terms.القربان: Sacrifice/offering — used by Ibrahim to disguise the nature of what he was about to do from Ismail until the moment of revelation
key_terms.المدية: The knife/blade — the implement Ibrahim used at the point of near-sacrifice
key_terms.المزدلفة: Muzdalifa — the station between Arafat and Mina; here etymologized from 'izdalafa' (to approach/move toward)
key_terms.المشعر الحرام: The Sacred Monument — the prominent spot at Muzdalifa where pilgrims offer du'a after departing from Arafat
key_terms.عرفات: Arafat — the plain outside Mecca where pilgrims gather on the 9th of Dhul-Hijja; here etymologized from 'arafa' (to know/acknowledge) and Ibrahim's confession of sins
key_terms.كابر عن كابر: From elder to elder — indicating continuous inheritance/succession of a practice

ai.seo_question: What is the story of Ibrahim's Hajj and the near-sacrifice of Ismail according to Imam al-Baqir and Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: This hadith preserves an extended narrative, transmitted from Imams al-Baqir and al-Sadiq (AS) through Abu Baseer, detailing the Hajj pilgrimage of Ibrahim (AS) as guided by Jibrail — including the naming of the key Hajj stations (al-Tarwiya, Arafat, al-Muzdalifa) and culminating in the divine command to sacrifice his son, Ismail (AS). The narrative showcases Ismail's willing submission to God's command and Ibrahim's unwavering obedience, with Jibrail intervening at the final moment to turn away the knife, and a ram being substituted. The account also describes how the wicked old man (Satan) tried to dissuade Ibrahim and then spread news to the old woman (Hajar), whose reaction upon seeing scratch marks on Ismail's neck led to the illness from which she died; it concludes with a note that this sacred spot was passed down through the Prophet's family until Ali ibn al-Husayn (AS).
word_analysis: and it never ceased to be
